Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 80, verse 17–32:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Let man be destroyed﴾, meaning: may he be cursed. By "man" here is meant the disbeliever. Regarding whom this statement refers to, there are three opinions.

The first: it refers to every disbeliever; this is the view of Mujahid. The second: it is Umayya ibn Khalaf; this is the view of al-Dahhak. The third: it is Utba ibn Abi Lahab; this is the view of Muqatil.

Regarding His saying, the Exalted: ﴿How disbelieving is he!﴾ there are three opinions.

The first: "How intense is his disbelief!" This is the view of Ibn Jurayj.

The second: "What is it that made him disbelieve?" This is the view of al-Suddi. According to this, it is a question of rebuke.

The third: it is in the form of wonder, and this wonder is something that human beings are commanded to feel, meaning: "Marvel, you all, at his disbelief." This is the view of al-Zajjaj.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿From what thing did He create him?﴾ Then He explained it, saying, the Exalted: ﴿From a drop of semen He created him﴾. Regarding the meaning of "fa-qaddarahu" (and He determined him) there are three opinions.

The first: He determined his limbs: his head, his two eyes, his two hands, and his two feet; this is the view of Ibn al-Sa'ib.

The second: He determined him in stages: a drop, then a clinging clot, until the end of his creation; this is the view of Muqatil.

The third: He determined him to be upright (in proportion); this is the view of al-Zajjaj.

﴿Then the way He made easy for him﴾. There are two opinions regarding this.

The first: He made the knowledge of the path of truth and falsehood easy for him; this is the view of al-Hasan and Mujahid. Al-Farra' said: the meaning is, "Then He made him easy for the path."

The second: He made the way easy for him in his emergence from his mother's womb; this is the view of al-Suddi and Muqatil.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then He caused him to be buried﴾. Al-Farra' said: that is, He made him one who is buried, and did not make him one of those who are thrown to the beasts and birds. So it is as if burial is among the honours bestowed upon the Muslim. He did not say "qabbarahu" (He had him buried), because the one who buries (qabir) is the one who buries with his own hand. The one who causes burial (muqbir) is God, because He made him one who is buried, so His action is not like the action of a human being. The Arabs say: "I cut off the tail of the camel (batartu dhanab al-ba'ir), and God cut it off entirely (abtarahu)"; "I cut the horn of the bull (ghadabtu qarn al-thawr), and God removed it (a'dabahu)"; "I drove so-and-so away from me (tardtu fulanan 'anni), and God drove him away (atradahu)," meaning: He made him an outcast. Abu 'Ubayda said: "aqbarahu" means: he ordered that he be buried, and provided him with a grave. The Banu Tamim said to 'Umar ibn Hubayra, when he killed Salih ibn 'Abd al-Rahman: "We have had Salih buried (aqbarna Salihan)." He said: "Take him, he is yours." The one who buries with his own hand is the qabir. Al-A'sha said:

"Had she leaned a dead man against her neck, he would have lived, and would not have been handed over to a gravedigger."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Then, when He wills, He will raise him up﴾, meaning: He will resurrect him. It is said: "Allah raised up the dead (anshara Allahu al-mawta), and they were raised up (fa-nshurū)," and "the dead man came back to life (nashara al-mayyit)," by himself, and its plural is nashir. Al-A'sha said:

"Until people say, at what they see: how marvellous is the dead one who rises!"

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Nay﴾. Al-Hasan said: truly. ﴿He has not yet fulfilled what He commanded him﴾, meaning by his Lord, and has not performed what was obligatory upon him. Is this general or specific? There are two opinions.

The first: it is general. Mujahid said: no one ever fulfills all that Allah has made obligatory upon him.

The second: it is specific to the disbeliever, who has not fulfilled what he was commanded of faith and obedience; this is the view of Yahya ibn Salam. When He mentioned the creation of the son of Adam, He mentioned his provision so that he would take heed and draw evidence for the resurrection from plants. He said, the Exalted: ﴿Then let man look at his food﴾. Muqatil said: he means by it Utba ibn Abi Lahab. The meaning of the speech: let man consider how Allah created his food, which He made a cause of his life. Then He explained, saying, the Exalted: ﴿That We﴾. Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir read "innā" with a kasra. 'Asim, Hamza and al-Kisa'i read "anna sababna" with a fatha on the hamza both in connection and at the beginning; Ruways agreed with them on the fatha in connection, but when he began, he used a kasra. Al-Zajjaj said: whoever reads "innā" with a kasra does so as a new beginning and resumption; whoever reads with a fatha does so as an apposition to "food," the meaning being: let man look at "that We poured water." The exegetes said: by pouring water he meant the rain. ﴿Then We split the earth﴾ with plants ﴿splitting﴾. ﴿And caused to grow therein grain﴾, meaning all the grains by which one is nourished; ﴿and grapes and clover (qadb)﴾. Al-Farra' said: it is the green fodder. The people of Makkah call qitt (fresh clover) "qadb." Ibn Qutayba said: it is said that it was named so because it is cut (yuqdab) again and again, that is, it is cut off; and likewise qasil, because it is cut (yuqsal), that is, cut off.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And olives and palm trees﴾ ﴿and thickly planted gardens (ghulban)﴾. Al-Farra' said: every orchard that has a wall around it is a ḥadīqa, and what does not have a wall is not called a ḥadīqa. Ghulb means: those thick with palms. Abu 'Ubayda said: it is said "shajara ghalbā'" when it is thick. Ibn Qutayba said: ghulb means: thick-necked. Al-Zajjaj said: they are the densely packed, large ones.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And fruit﴾, meaning: all kinds of fruit, ﴿and pasture (abban)﴾. There are two opinions regarding it.

The first: it is what the beasts graze on; this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ikrima and the philologists. Al-Zajjaj said: it is all the herbage which livestock feed upon.

The second: it is the fresh fruits; this is related by al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So when the Ṣākhkha (the deafening blast) comes﴾. It is the second blast.

Ibn Qutayba said: "Al-ṣākhkha (the deafening blast) deafens with a ṣakhkh, that is, it makes deaf. It is said: a man is aṣakh or aṣlakh if he does not hear. Calamity (al-dāhiya) is also called ṣākhkha."

Al-Zajjāj said: "It is the blast by which the Resurrection will take place. It deafens the ears, that is, it makes them deaf, so that they hear nothing except that by which they are called to be revived."

Then he explained when it will come, saying the Exalted: ﴿On the Day when a person will flee from his brother﴾. The exegetes (al-mufassirūn) said: the meaning is that a person will not turn to any of his relatives, because of the magnitude of what he is in.

Al-Ḥasan said: "The first to be fled from by his brother is Hābīl (Abel), and from his mother and father, Ibrāhīm (Abraham); from his companion, Nūḥ (Noah) and Lūṭ (Lot); and from his son, Nūḥ (Noah)."

Qatāda said: "Hābīl flees from Qābīl (Cain), the Prophet (ﷺ) flees from his mother, Ibrāhīm from his father, Lūṭ from his companion, and Nūḥ from his son."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For every person among them on that Day, there is a matter that will occupy him﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: "That is, it will preoccupy him away from his relatives." Ibn Qutayba said: "That is, it will divert him and keep him away from his relatives. It is said: ughnin ʿannī wajhaka (turn your face away from me), meaning: divert it; and ughnin ʿannī al-safīh (keep the fool away from me)."

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Zuhrī, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, Ibn Muḥaysin, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla recited yaʿnīhi (with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and an unpointed ʿayn), which means: "it will concern him," meaning it will engage him. Likewise, the reading of the one who recited yughnīhi with a ghayn means: he has a matter which, in view of it, nothing else concerns him.

It has been narrated from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: "ʿĀʾisha said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Will we be gathered naked?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Alas, my shame!' So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿For every person among them on that Day, there is a matter that will occupy him﴾."

Muqātil said: that is, blackness and gloom. ﴿Darkness will cover them﴾, that is, obscurity will overspread them. Al-Zajjāj said: "Blackness like smoke will rise over them."

Then he explained who the people of this state are, saying the Exalted: ﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾. It is the plural of kāfir (disbeliever) and fājir (wicked).

Al-Ḥasan said: "The first to be fled from by his brother is Hābīl (Abel), and from his mother and father, Ibrāhīm (Abraham); from his companion, Nūḥ (Noah) and Lūṭ (Lot); and from his son, Nūḥ (Noah)."

Qatāda said: "Hābīl flees from Qābīl (Cain), the Prophet (ﷺ) flees from his mother, Ibrāhīm from his father, Lūṭ from his companion, and Nūḥ from his son."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For every person among them on that Day, there is a matter that will occupy him﴾. Al-Farrāʾ said: "That is, it will preoccupy him away from his relatives." Ibn Qutayba said: "That is, it will divert him and keep him away from his relatives. It is said: ughnin ʿannī wajhaka (turn your face away from me), meaning: divert it; and ughnin ʿannī al-safīh (keep the fool away from me)."

Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, al-Zuhrī, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Ibn al-Sumayfaʿ, Ibn Muḥaysin, and Ibn Abī ʿAbla recited yaʿnīhi (with a fatḥa on the yāʾ and an unpointed ʿayn), which means: "it will concern him," meaning it will engage him. Al-Zajjāj said: "The meaning of the verse is: he has a concern which, while he is preoccupied with it, he is unable to attend to anything else." Likewise, the reading of the one who recited yughnīhi with a ghayn means: he has a matter which, in view of it, nothing else concerns him.

It has been narrated from Anas ibn Mālik, who said: "ʿĀʾisha said to the Prophet (ﷺ): 'Will we be gathered naked?' He said: 'Yes.' She said: 'Alas, my shame!' So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿For every person among them on that Day, there is a matter that will occupy him﴾."

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Faces on that Day will be bright﴾, that is, shining, having known what good is theirs. ﴿Laughing﴾ for their joy. ﴿Rejoicing﴾, that is, glad at what they have attained of the honour of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And faces on that Day will have dust upon them﴾, that is, dust. Muqātil said: that is, blackness and gloom. ﴿Darkness will cover them﴾, that is, obscurity will overspread them. Al-Zajjāj said: "Blackness like smoke will rise over them."

Then he explained who the people of this state are, saying the Exalted: ﴿Those are the disbelievers, the wicked﴾. It is the plural of kāfir (disbeliever) and fājir (wicked).
